title: Battle of Salamis
summary: The Greek fleet defeats Xerxes' navy at Salamis in the same campaign season as Thermopylae (Herodotus 8.40–96).
description: Added from the Herodotus import (The Histories, tr. Rawlinson). The sort year is derived from a CFAH anchor point (see the sort note); Herodotus entries are display only.

sorting_basis.note: Sort year copied from Xerxes invades Greece (CFAH AP-13, 480 BC). Herodotus puts the Persian entry into Attica four months after the crossing of the Hellespont, "in the archonship of Calliades" (8.51), and Salamis follows within days (8.56–96), so the battle falls in the invasion's first campaign season. Herodotus gives no year number.

chronologies.date: “a space of four months had gone by; one, while the army made the crossing, and delayed about the region of the Hellespont; and three while they proceeded thence to Attica, which they entered in the archonship of Calliades”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 8.51 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 536 (PDF p. 538)
chronologies.note: Herodotus dates by the Athenian archon; he does not number the year. Within CFAH AP-13 (480 BC).

chronologies.date: “At the dawn of day, all the menat-arms were assembled together”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 8.83 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 548 (PDF p. 550)
chronologies.note: The morning of the battle (the PDF prints "menat-arms" for "men-at-arms").

chronologies.date: “he thought it best to winter in Thessaly, and wait for the spring before he attempted the Peloponnese”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 8.113 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 561 (PDF p. 563)
chronologies.note: Mardonius winters in Thessaly after Salamis; the land war resumes the next year. DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): The next spring is 479 BC (CFAH AP-13 480 BC + 1).
